title: Titans sign All-Pro DT Jeffery Simmons to contract extension
content:
The Tennessee Titans have agreed to a three-year contract extension with star defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons, the team announced Friday. The new deal is worth $105.8 million, including $100 million guaranteed, according to multiple reports, and keeps Simmons in Tennessee through the 2030 season.

Simmons, who will turn 29 in July, has been one of the few bright spots for the Titans in recent years. He is a four-time Pro Bowler who also earned first-team All-Pro honors in 2025 after being named second-team All-Pro in 2021 and 2022. After beginning his rookie season recovering from a torn ACL while training for the draft, Simmons has been very durable. Over the past six seasons, he’s started at least 15 games five times. His 2025 season was the best of his career, setting career-highs across the board. He tallied 11 sacks, 17 tackles for loss, 21 quarterback hits and three forced fumbles.

For his career, Simmons has 42.5 sacks. His 37.5 sacks since 2021 rank 10th among all defensive linemen.

“Tennessee has become a second home for me,” Simmons told the team website. “From day one, this organization believed in me, and I’m grateful for the opportunity to continue to pour into this franchise and community. I want to thank God, my family, my teammates, Ms. Amy and the entire Titans organization for believing in me. My job isn’t finished. I believe in this locker room and this staff, and I’m focused on helping this team get back to competing for championships.”

Simmons is one of the few carryovers from the team’s winning years under former head coach Mike Vrabel. The Titans went to the conference championship in Simmons’ rookie season and made the playoffs each of the following two years. The team has missed the playoffs in each of the last four seasons and is coming off back-to-back three-win campaigns. The Titans also made a change at head coach, going from the offensive-minded Brian Callahan in 2024 to bringing in former San Francisco 49ers defensive coordinator Robert Saleh this offseason.

Simmons had two years remaining on a four-year extension he signed with the Titans in 2023. The new deal ensures that Simmons will be in Tennessee for the duration of his prime.
